label: D2: chose a1, reached S1 (common), after a rewarded previous trial
explanation: Fires only at D2 and only when the agent chose a1 and reached S1 by a common transition. It never fires at D1 or GO, on S2 or after a2 (78 of 80k activations), or after rare transitions. Requiring that the previous trial was rewarded (the reward shown at this trial s D1) lifts precision from 0.62 to 0.89 at dev F1 0.91 and mass recall 0.98. All variables are observed by D2 (choice, state, and the previous reward), so no future variable is used. Magnitude grows over runs of consecutive rewarded a1->S1 common trials (about 0.3-0.6 after one, near max after several), so it looks like accumulated evidence that S1 is good, i.e. a1 is worth repeating. It is weak or silent on the first a1->S1c trial after a switch from a2, a rare transition, or an unrewarded trial. The missed activations are small and come from a1->S1c trials after an unrewarded trial that follow a rewarded streak. Adding good == 1 hurts recall (F1 0.84), so the feature tracks the observed streak, not the hidden good state.

issues: The phase, choice and transition claims hold. All activation is at D2 (0 at D1 or GO). Outside a1->S1 common at D2 the predicate covers 0.03% of activations (78 steps). Without the reward term, D2 & a1 & common has dev precision 0.62 and recall 0.999.

Systematic false positive: 'after a rewarded previous trial' is too broad. The reward has to have been earned at S1. For D2 & a1 & common & prev_reward==1 & prev_state==2 (the last trial was rewarded at S2), the feature fires on 0 of 4870 predicted dev steps. The rewarded-a1-rare case (prev_action==1 & prev_common==0, which ends at S2) is also 0 of 4855. These steps make up most of the predicate's false positives.

Replacing prev_reward==1 with prev_reward==1 & prev_state!=2 removes that class. prev_state is -1 (unknown) on the window's first trial, which is why the test uses !=2 rather than ==1. Dev precision rises from 0.887 to 0.941 and dev F1 from 0.915 to 0.942. Test precision rises from 0.877 to 0.931 and test F1 from 0.907 to 0.935, with recall unchanged (0.939) and mass recall unchanged (0.977).

The remaining test false positives are mostly the first rewarded-S1 trial after a non-S1 or unrewarded history, where the feature is still warming up. This fits the explanation's point that magnitude grows over a streak.

The remaining misses are small (2.3% of activation mass). They are a1->S1c trials after an unrewarded trial that follow a rewarded-S1 streak, as the explanation says. Treat these as scattered or decaying residue, not a separate class.
The predicate uses no future variables, so that claim is fine.
